steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Quantitative data: numerical, can be statistically analysed. Qualitative data: descriptive, words rather than numbers. Primary data: collected by the researcher. Secondary data: collected by someone else for a different purpose.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Measures of central tendency: Mean (average - affected by outliers), Median (middle value - not affected by outliers), Mode (most common - useful for categorical data). Measures of dispersion: Range (highest minus lowest - simple but affected by outliers), Standard deviation (average distance from the mean - more precise but complex).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Data presentation: bar charts (discrete/categorical data), histograms (continuous data, no gaps between bars), scatter graphs (correlations), tables (organised raw data). Choose the presentation method that best represents the data type.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethical issues: informed consent (participants must agree to take part), deception (misleading participants - only acceptable if justified and debriefed), protection from harm (physical and psychological), privacy (right to confidentiality), right to withdraw (participants can leave at any time).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between quantitative and qualitative data, giving one strength and one limitation of each. | Describe three ethical issues that psychologists must consider when conducting research. | A study finds mean = 15, median = 12, mode = 10. Explain what these results suggest about the distribution of the data.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Mean = average (affected by outliers). Median = middle (not affected by outliers). Mode = most common. Informed consent + Right to withdraw + Debriefing = the ethical minimum for any study. Bar chart = categorical data (gaps between bars). Histogram = continuous data (no gaps).
